title: Seahawks expected to sign former Lions CB Terrion Arnold amid legal troubles: Source
author: Saad Yousuf
content:
The Seattle Seahawks are expected to sign former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold, a league source told The Athletic on condition of anonymity because the deal hasn’t been finalized. A first-round pick in 2024, Arnold was released by the Lions on June 29, less than a week after he was arrested on charges of kidnapping and robbery.

Arnold voluntarily surrendered himself to authorities June 24 at Orient Road Jail in Tampa, Fla. He faces four counts of kidnapping and four counts of armed robbery, which carry a potential sentence of up to life in prison.

Arnold was initially held without bond, but Judge Christopher C. Sabella set Arnold’s bail at $1 million less than a week later. Sabella also denied the prosecution’s attempt to require Arnold to wear an ankle monitor after Arnold’s attorney, Harvey Steinberg, argued the mandate would have effectively prevented him from playing in the NFL.

Despite the pending legal trouble, Arnold garnered interest from multiple NFL teams. He had visits with the Seahawks, Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints and New York Giants.

During an episode of HBO’s “Hard Knocks” that aired Tuesday, two scenes showed the Seahawks’ interest in Arnold, including his workout at the team’s facility. General manager John Schneider suggested the Seahawks expect Arnold to be permitted to play during the preseason. It’s unclear whether the NFL will place Arnold on the commissioner’s exempt list, which would make him ineligible.

Arnold was a standout cornerback at Alabama before the Lions moved up in the draft to select him in the first round in 2024. In two seasons with the Lions, he played in 24 games and recorded one interception. He appeared in 16 games as a rookie but was limited to eight games last season due to injury, including a shoulder issue that ended his season.

According to court documents, Arnold is due to appear in court in person on Oct. 5.

The first of two “Hard Knocks” scenes on the Seahawks’ interest in Arnold adequately captured the team’s thought process. In addition to doing due diligence on Arnold’s legal situation, Schneider relayed to coach Mike Macdonald that he sought insight from quarterback Jalen Milroe, Arnold’s college teammate. Milroe gave a strong endorsement, Schneider said.

Although Schneider ultimately makes the final call, he has long valued players’ opinions (defensive backs coach Karl Scott also has history with Arnold). Schneider’s priority is ensuring a good fit from a personality and attitude standpoint. — Michael-Shawn Dugar

Seattle let starting cornerback Riq Woolen walk in free agency, then signed free-agent cornerback Noah Igbinoghene, used a third-round pick on Julian Neal and seventh-round picks on Andre Fuller and Michael Dansby. The Seahawks also re-signed Shemar Jean-Charles and Josh Jobe, the latter on a $24 million deal (Seattle’s rotation also features 2024 fifth-round pick Nehemiah Pritchett).

They don’t need another corner, necessarily, but the Seahawks believe Arnold is worth a flier based on what he’s put on tape relative to the rest of Seattle’s depth chart. — Dugar
